Functional requirements Description of what the digital system needs to do to support the tasks that make up the health system process and address the identified challenges (e.g., a product master data management solution must be able to define categories and attributes to organize product information).
Non-functional requirements Description of the attributes and constraints that the system must have to ensure its quality and performance.
These requirements do not specify what the system should do, but rather how the system should perform its functions.

SMART Guidelines are a structured approach to integrating recommended public health and clinical practices into digital systems.
They represent the WHO’s approach to systematising and accelerating the consistent application of recommended, life-saving interventions in the digital age.
L1 – Narrative: enhanced clinical, public health guidelines and structured data recommendations.

16  Instituting data management and governance policies For effective use of data in operations, analysis, and decision-making, the integrity and quality of data must be consistently and continuously maintained.
Data management policies should ensure adherence to principles of privacy, security, and ethical data usage.
It is important to note that the steps might not always follow a linear order and may be implemented simultaneously or concurrently.

Instituting data management and governance policies   17 *Master data management procedures should include the following key elements to continuously and securely maintain master data: • Data governance framework: Establish clear policies, roles, responsibilities, and processes to ensure data quality and consistency for use across the health supply chain.

The data owner: - Defines the rules, policies, and standards for data quality, structure, and governance. - Makes decisions on how the data should be managed and ensures alignment with business objectives. - Approves changes to the product master data and ensures compliance with regulatory and business requirements. - Is accountable for the accuracy, completeness, and relevance of the product data in the organization. - Data custodian: responsible for the technical management and security of product master data.

18  Instituting data management and governance policies INPUTS STEPS RESOURCES OUTPUTS • Data harmonization activities plan • Master data management procedures including master data governance policies Conduct data harmonization activities such as establishing a standardized coding scheme, master data definitions and structures* to organize and maintain master data consistently and persistently • Data harmonization activities must consider all sources of product data, as well as the systems, processes, and organizations or stakeholders that will utilize this data.

Instituting data management and governance policies   19 *Master data definitions and structures should include provisions for maintaining product classifications, generic product information, and trade item details.

9: Relationship between generic product, trade item and regulated trade item Best practices: • It is generally recommended to avoid including product classification or product characteristics such as dosage and strength in the generic national product code.

Instead, a system-generated sequential numeric or alphanumeric code should be used. • Product characteristics such as dosage, strength, pack size, and route of administration should be defined as attributes and linked to the product codes.

This combination of attributes and codes facilitates comprehensive identification of products. • Generic national product codes, including drug codes and medicinal product identifiers (when using the WHO Drug Dictionary), should be mapped to trade item-specific identifiers, such as GTINs, or similar unique identifiers where GTINs are not available. • The product coding system should maintain uniform code lengths and ensure scalability to accommodate an increasing number of unique products. • Product master data structures should support the mapping of one generic national product code to multiple corresponding trade items.

In addition, the data structure should organize multiple packaging levels and quantity relationships across those. • Packaging hierarchies and quantity conversions across these levels—along with packaging variations among different brand items—are critical for countries to effectively manage supply chain operations such as inventory control and distribution.
To address these concerns, procedures and systems should be developed to categorize data attributes based on their level of sensitivity.
Access should then be controlled according to these sensitivity categories, ensuring appropriate data protection while enabling secure data sharing.

Establish a master data governance group composed of all relevant stakeholders to provide leadership and guidance in managing product master data additions and changes. • The governance group should support the overall governance and planning of product master data standardization, capture, and dissemination activities, and provide leadership and oversight for all data management efforts. • The master data governance group can be integrated into existing governance structures or steering committees.
